news.title: 'Falklands issue was a special ingredient': Lautaro lifts lid on Argentina’s World Cup grudge match against England
news.lede: Lautaro Martinez has revealed how Argentina’s long-running dispute with England over the Falkland Islands added an emotional edge to their 2026 World Cup semifinal, describing the clash as far more than a football match and dedicating his decisive goal to veterans of the 1982 war. The Inter Milan striker scored a 92nd-minute winner as Argentina came from behind to beat England 2-1 in Atlanta on July 15, booking their place in a second consecutive World Cup final. The goal has since taken on a significance beyond the result, particularly among Argentines who continue to regard the conflict over the islands as a defining chapter in their national history. In an interview with AFA Estudio, Martinez became emotional when shown footage of a Malvinas War veteran breaking down in tears while celebrating his goal.

news.title: CommBank ParaMatildas defeat Netherlands 13-0 to finish IFCPF Women’s World Cup group stage on a high
news.lede: The CommBank ParaMatildas have finished their group stage campaign with a 13-0 victory over the Netherlands. Annmarie de Uriarte added five to her considerable goal-scoring total, while Trinity McPhie scored a hat-trick, Lainee Harrison and Katelyn Smith struck braces, and Leah Spaine put away her fifth of the tournament. The result means that Australia has finished top of Group B and will take on Finland, who finished second in Group A, in the semi-finals. There were three changes to the starting five that defeated Colombia last time out.

news.title: Football Ferns to end 2026 with home series against Philippines
news.lede: As the Football Ferns gathered for a team meeting to name the squad to play Panama, they were interrupted by violent shaking. A magnitude 7.7 earthquake struck southern Panama on Friday, damaging homes, cutting power, halting flights and sending residents into the streets, while triggering more than a dozen aftershocks. Football Ferns coach Michael Mayne said it was a scary moment for the squad. "We felt the biggest shake.

news.title: Football Ferns book Porirua Park for two-match series against Philippines
news.lede: The Football Ferns will complete their 2026 international programme with two matches against the Philippines at Wellington’s Porirua Park. The games, on Sunday November 29 and Friday December 4, will provide more preparation for next year’s FIFA Women’s World Cup in Brazil. The Philippines are ranked #39 in the FIFA women’s world rankings and will provide opposition for coach Michael Mayne’s side, who are #32. The series follows the cancellation of New Zealand’s planned October internationals against Panama after an earthquake struck the Central American country.

news.title: Football: Soccer-FIFA suspends coach Hassan and forward Zico for three and five matches
news.lede: Oct 19 (Reuters) - FIFA has ⁠suspended Egypt coach Hossam Hassan and forward Mostafa Zico ⁠for three and five matches respectively, the Egyptian Football ‌Association said on Monday, after theycriticisedthe referee following a 3-2 defeat by Argentina in the World Cup. The 60-year-old Hassan was sanctioned after blaming refereeing errors ​for his country's elimination from the ⁠tournament in the last 16, ⁠whileZico insulted the referee in a post-match interview. Ibrahim Hassan, Hossam's twin ⁠brother ‌and Egypt's national team director, has also been suspended for three matches. "The decisions include the suspension of ⁠Hossam Hassan and Ibrahim Hassan for three matches ​each, while Zico ‌has been suspended for five matches," the EFA said ⁠in a ​statement.

news.title: Uefa demands Fifa releases documents relating to World Cup sell-off scheme
news.lede: European governing body gives two-week deadline. Letter addresses other issues including Balogun affair. Uefa has given Fifa a two-week deadline to release key documents relating to Gianni Infantino’s World Cup sell-off plan and other governance issues in its latest critique of football’s world governing body. A letter sent to Fifa’s general secretary, Mattias Grafström, by his counterpart at Uefa, Theodore Theodoridis, is accompanied by an eight-page document that has more than 50 questions about Fifa’s handling of dozens of issues over the past 12 months.
